translation_notes: context shim: local vstore.py replaces the VIVO SPARQLStore/SPARQLUpdateStore package (no live VIVO endpoint); same constructor and open((query, update)) contract, backed by rdflib's in-memory store, so every graph operation of the region really runs; the `from vstore import ...` line is unchanged on both sides
the driver supplies the three VIVO_* environment variables the script reads

flagship case: the inline Turtle document passed to g.parse(data="""...""", format='turtle') becomes a g{...} island -- Graph() + parse() collapse into `g = g{...}`, the five @prefix lines of the document become five ldpy @prefix statements (xml: and xsd: are unused, kept to mirror the document), and the Turtle body is copied verbatim inside the island
validated: stdout is identical, including print(g.serialize(format='n3')) and the ordered `Concept: ...` listing, so the island materialises the same triples in the same order as the Turtle parser

URIRef('http://example.org/...') -> <http://example.org/...> (2 occurrences); RDF.type/SKOS.Concept/RDFS.label -> rdf:type/skos:Concept/rdfs:label (6 occurrences), including inside keyword arguments and Resource.set calls

`from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, RDF, Literal` reduced to `Graph, Literal` and `from rdflib.namespace import SKOS, RDFS` dropped (absorbed by the @prefix declarations); Literal stays because Literal("Baseball") appears outside any island, where ldpy does no coercion

negative finding: outside islands ldpy adds nothing to the graph-API calls -- named_graph.remove((s, p, o)), Resource.set(p, o) and .value(...) keep their tuple/argument shape; only the term notation improves there
